search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; adaptive reused-development selection; fresh-audit e-processes; predictable side-information betting; selection complexity versus evidence capital; misspecification robustness

public_sources.title: Safe testing
public_sources.authors: Peter Grunwald; Rianne de Heide; Wouter Koolen
public_sources.used_scope: Conditional e-variables may be designed just in time from information available before the next fresh batch while products remain test supermartingales. Used to justify development-data side information for choosing the next fresh bet, not development outcomes as fresh evidence.

public_sources.title: E-backtesting
public_sources.authors: Qiuqi Wang; Ruodu Wang; Johanna Ziegel
public_sources.used_scope: Any predictable betting process in the stated range preserves the supermartingale validity of their e-process, while power depends strongly on the bet; when the alternative is unknown they discuss empirical and mixture approaches. Used as external support for separating validity of predictable betting from alternative-model quality.

public_sources.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
public_sources.used_scope: Complete-class result for finitely conditionally constrained hypotheses: arbitrary e-processes are pointwise dominated by predictable products of affine one-step e-variables. Used only as structural support for prioritizing predictable one-step fresh bets under the applicable conditional sign constraint.

public_sources.title: What Fits (Into Few Tokens) Doesn't Overfit: Compression and Generalization in ML Research Agents
public_sources.authors: Martin Andres Bertran; Aaron Roth; Zhiwei Steven Wu
public_sources.used_scope: Research-agent validation reuse with a one-bit improvement transcript. Used as the external adaptive-proposal setting motivating explicit separation between development-side information and genuinely fresh confirmation evidence.

fresh_side_information_betting.setup: Let D be arbitrarily reused development data and let h(D) be the frozen selected candidate. On fresh paired tasks, conditional on D and prior fresh outcomes, suppose a discordant sign obeys P(+ | D, fresh past, discordant)<=1/2 under the selected-candidate null. Choose any predictable q_t in [1/2,1] as a function of D and fresh past.
fresh_side_information_betting.one_step_factor: Use factor 2 q_t for candidate-only success, 2(1-q_t) for incumbent-only success, and 1 for concordance.
fresh_side_information_betting.validity: Conditional on discordance, expected factor is 2[(1-q_t)+p_t(2q_t-1)]<=1 for p_t<=1/2 and q_t>=1/2; concordance contributes factor 1. Therefore the product is a conditional e-process even if q_t uses arbitrary frozen development-side information. No transcript-complexity charge is needed merely for choosing the fresh bet, because D is side information rather than reused evidence in the factor.
fresh_side_information_betting.scope_guard: The candidate must be frozen before the fresh outcome used by each factor, and the conditional sign-null must remain true after selection. This does not make reused development outcomes themselves fresh evidence.

selected_global_evalue_is_not_effect_siz.statement: The selection-corrected global reuse e-value S=pi(U)E_U combines raw reused evidence E_U with transcript/selection prior mass pi(U). Its magnitude need not be monotone in the probability or size of a genuine effect.
selected_global_evalue_is_not_effect_siz.simulator_explanation: In the adaptive proposal loop, later/more informative transcripts make genuinely good selected candidates more likely but also receive much smaller pi(U). This can make small S correspond to stronger candidates. Therefore using larger S as a monotone instruction to bet more aggressively can be badly miscalibrated even though S remains a valid e-value.
selected_global_evalue_is_not_effect_siz.operational_rule: For fresh bet selection, retain the frozen decomposition/raw features that are validation-independent at audit time, such as raw candidate e-evidence, transcript complexity, stop class and record count. Use S itself for evidential capital only when the protocol deliberately chooses to do so.

conditional_product_scope_narrowing.prior_result_preserved: For a fixed valid transform h(S), h(S)F_t is anytime-valid and pathwise dominates the earlier convex merger using the same h when the convex merger crosses later.
conditional_product_scope_narrowing.new_narrowing: This does not imply h(S)F_t dominates fresh-only F_t. Whenever h(S)<1, the product starts with less than one unit of fresh-audit wealth and delays every otherwise identical fresh crossing. In the full adaptive loop S was below 1 on about 98.93% of alternative trajectories, so common-path capital taxation outweighed rare large-S reuse gains for true-resolution rate at budgets 50-200.
conditional_product_scope_narrowing.consequence: When selection-corrected reused evidence is weak, prefer development information as a predictor of the fresh bet rather than automatically reinvesting it as starting capital.

hedged_predictive_bet.construction: On disjoint meta-simulations fit p_hat(D)=P(selected candidate is genuinely good | frozen pre-audit features). For a training effect q_good=.75 use q_pred=.5+.25 p_hat. A fixed protocol hedge q_half=.5*.75+.5*q_pred remains predictable and hence null-valid regardless of predictor accuracy.
hedged_predictive_bet.scope_guard: Prediction misspecification affects finite-horizon power and audit cost, not the conditional null-validity proof. The reported predictor and hedge are worker-local simulation devices, not externally validated effect models.

worker_local_full_loop_simulation.purpose: Execute the prior checkpoint's exact next action and stress conditional-product starting wealth plus development-informed fresh betting. These are finite Monte Carlo results for a stylized loop, not deployed-agent performance claims.

proposal_loop.candidate_generation: At proposal t, P(good)=min(0.02+0.10*record_count,0.45); bad candidates have q=.5. Stop regimes and transcript prior are inherited from the prior evaluation checkpoint. Selected candidate is the largest fixed-horizon reused-dev paired-sign e-value.
proposal_loop.selection_prior: Validation-independent robust transcript mixture from prior checkpoint; learned weights fixed before these evaluation runs.

selected_global_S_distribution_independe.interpretation: Reuse capital was weak on almost all paths despite the selected candidate being genuinely good on about 44% of paths.

starting_wealth_transform_grid.transforms: affine h_a=1-a+aS for a in {0,.05,.1,.2,.4,.6,.8,1}; power S^gamma for gamma in {.1,.2,.35,.5,.7,.85,1}; four fixed affine/power mixtures
starting_wealth_transform_grid.null_sanity: Across rho=.2/.4/.6 and 50k null selection trajectories, maximum B200 crossing was 0.04114 for fresh-only, 0.03324 for affine a=.2 and 0.02472 for affine a=.4, all below alpha=.05. Validity follows from the proof; simulation is only a sanity check.
starting_wealth_transform_grid.interpretation: Conditional-product reuse starting wealth provides a smooth true-resolution versus false/harmful-commit frontier but did not improve average true resolution or audit cost over fresh-only in this weak-S full loop. The earlier conditional-S=5 gains therefore do not generalize to the unconditional selected-S distribution.

preaudit_predictor.training: 120k disjoint adaptive-loop meta trajectories; evaluation on an independent 40k selection trajectories.
preaudit_predictor.diagnostic: In the training meta-run the smallest-S decile had about 96.1% genuinely-good selected candidates, while several middle/high S deciles were only about 28-39% good. This directly falsifies monotone 'larger S means stronger effect' inside this simulator.

strategies.decomp: q_t=.5+.25*p_hat(raw evidence, transcript complexity, stop time, record count)
strategies.decomp_half: 50/50 protocol-fixed hedge between .75 and decomposed q_t

null_sanity_60k.interpretation: All were below .05; the proof, not Monte Carlo, provides validity. Development-informed bet choice stayed null-valid despite being highly data-dependent because the fresh factor was predictable.

misspecification_stress.deliberately_inverted_feature_to_fresh_e: Set good-candidate fresh q approximately 0.51+0.28*(1-p_hat_decomp), so features that caused aggressive learned bets now predicted weaker fresh transfer. At B50 fixed true-commit was 0.03725 versus 0.02585 for decomp_half; at B200 fixed was 0.08095 versus 0.08548. Thus predictable side-information betting keeps validity under severe misspecification but can lose short-horizon power; hedge choice must be evaluated under transfer shift, not only in-distribution calibration.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use arbitrarily adaptive reused-development information only to choose the predictable betting strategy for genuinely fresh paired confirmation; keep fresh e-process starting wealth at one unless reused evidence is deliberately admitted as capital.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct conditional-factor proof; Safe Testing; E-backtesting; Clerico 2026 structural result; worker-local null and alternative stress tests.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires frozen candidate and fresh conditional sign-null after selection.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For fresh bet selection, retain raw evidence and selection-complexity/transcript features rather than collapsing them to S=pi E and then treating S magnitude as an effect proxy.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local disjoint-meta prediction AUC .974 versus .714 for S-only and large finite-budget false-commit reduction with preserved long-horizon true resolution.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Predictive utility is simulator-specific; validity does not depend on this predictor being calibrated, but power does.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Before multiplying fresh evidence by h(S), measure the realized distribution of selection-corrected S. If h(S)<1 on nearly all paths, product reinvestment can be a capital tax; side-information-only use of D may dominate for finite-budget resolution.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Full-loop transform grid: S>1 only 1.07% under the simulated alternative; fresh-only had higher true resolution and lower mean audit time than positive affine/power reinvestment at budgets 50-200, while reinvestment reduced harmful/false commits.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Does not overturn conditional-product validity or conditional gains when S is materially above one.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use a protocol-fixed hedge between a robust baseline fresh bet and a disjoint-meta learned pre-audit predictor. This can capture weak-effect gains while reducing harmful/false commits, without data-dependent top-level evidence weighting.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Across q=.60-.80/rho=.2-.6 at B200, the 50/50 hedge slightly increased aggregate true commits 0.31984->0.32313 while reducing harmful/false commits 0.02176->0.01376; under deliberate inverted transfer it lost short-horizon power, establishing a clear robustness boundary.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: The 50/50 number is not universal and must be tuned only from validation-independent meta-data or covered by a separate validity-preserving online strategy.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'because h(S)F_t is valid and dominates the previous convex merger, it should replace fresh-only F_t.' Dominance was only versus the convex merger with the same starting transform; h(S)<1 can make it strictly worse than fresh-only on common paths.

Rejected in the full-loop simulator: 'larger selection-corrected S means the selected candidate is more likely genuinely good.' S mixed raw evidence with a complexity penalty and was strongly non-monotone as an effect predictor.

Narrowed: 'adaptive reused-development information must always pay selection complexity before it can influence fresh confirmation.' It must pay if reused outcomes become evidential capital, but it can be used freely as predictable side information for a conditionally valid fresh factor.

Narrowed: 'predictor misspecification threatens Type-I validity.' Under the stated sign-null it threatens growth/power, not validity; deliberate inverted-transfer stress produced large short-horizon power loss without changing the conditional e-process proof.

frontier.action: Replace the point pre-audit q predictor with a validation-independent mixture over fresh alternative strengths q in roughly [.55,.80], allowing fresh outcomes to update mixture weights predictably. Compare fixed .75, decomp_half and mixture betting under aligned, weak-transfer and inverted-transfer regimes.

Add shared-task difficulty, cross-candidate task correlation and heterogeneous discordance to the full proposal/fresh-audit simulator. Verify conditional sign-null statements explicitly rather than assuming independent candidate/task draws.

Replace reused fixed-horizon candidate e-values with actual anytime PACE paths. Account for candidate selection that can inspect within-candidate stopping time/supremum and determine whether adjusters or a different selected-global e-value are required.
Stress repeated candidate streams and multiple accepted modifications using e-process multiple-testing/adjuster results; separate per-candidate fresh validity from run-level FWER/FDR.

Characterize when weak reused evidence should be used only for bet prediction, versus admitted as starting capital through a predeclared transform or exact-risk branch, using finite-budget decision utility rather than log-growth alone.

exact_next_action: Construct a fresh sign e-process with a disjoint-meta prior/mixture over alternative strengths and pre-audit feature classes, update it predictably on fresh outcomes, and stress it against fixed .75 and decomp_half under weak/inverted transfer plus shared-task heterogeneity before moving reused selection from fixed-horizon e-values to actual PACE suprema.
